title: Dojo's Node and Python render orders disagree on an arm whose engine is null
body:
## Summary
packages/producers/src/dojo/plan.ts `localOrder` and pipeline/foundry/dojo_video_h3.py `order` sort a serial-lane spec differently when an arm carries `"engine": null` (and Node's mediaOf and localOrder disagree with each other on `""`).

## Description
localOrder (packages/producers/src/dojo/plan.ts:88) reads `(u.engine ?? "wan") === "wan"`: null -> wan, "" -> H3. The Python runner's engine_of (pipeline/foundry/dojo_video_h3.py:48-49) is `p[arm].get("engine", "wan")`: a present null is None, sorted with H3 and rendered with the H3 workflow (:85). mediaOf (plan.ts:48) treats both null and "" as 'no engine'. The plan's local units (lib/producers/dojo.ts:136 localUnits) are claimed to be 'in the runner's own render order'; for these specs they are not. Fixed: one rule on both sides - null and "" mean the default engine (wan) - held by a plan-cases.json-style case both languages run.

## Flow
- a serial-lane gen-spec with one arm `engine: null` and another arm `engine: "h3-ref2va"`
- Node localOrder -> [p1--baseline, p2--baseline, p1--challenger, p2--challenger]
- Python order -> [p2--baseline, p1--baseline, p1--challenger, p2--challenger], and p1--baseline rendered with the H3 workflow
- fix: Python engine_of -> `p[arm].get("engine") or "wan"`; Node -> `(u.engine || "wan")`; add the case to dojo/plan-cases.json and both runners of it

## Expected impact
The operator's receipt and step list name the order the card actually renders in; a null engine stops silently buying a ~70 min H3 first-load. Could break: a spec that relied on null meaning H3 (none found).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the Node plan and the Python runner order one spec the same way
Before: 1 literal spec (null engine on one arm): the two orders differ (probed: python -I over dojo_video_h3.order vs localOrder's rule)
After: same spec, both sides `null|"" -> wan`: identical order
Method: probe - both sides run on one literal spec; the fix spans pipeline/foundry (outside this context), so it cannot land here
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
pipeline/foundry/dojo_video_h3.py:49  return p[arm].get("engine", "wan")
packages/producers/src/dojo/plan.ts:88  (u.engine ?? "wan") === "wan"
probe: python order -> ['p2--baseline', 'p1--baseline', 'p1--challenger', 'p2--challenger']
instrument: a dojo/plan-cases.json case with engine null and "" run by tests/next-server/producer-dojo.test.ts through both localOrder and dojo_video_h3.order

title: A dojo google call that throws after reaching the vendor books no spend row
body:
## Summary
packages/producers/src/dojo/define.ts `metered` books entries only when `live()` returns; a generate or readback that throws leaves no ledger row, and the kernel books nothing either because the meter was used.

## Description
metered (dojo/define.ts:68-85) calls ctx.meter.paid(JOB_USD, ...) whose entries come from the live result only (packages/kernel/src/spend/meter.ts:113-130). JOB_USD has no ceiling, so nothing is held; a thrown live call returns no entries and `paid` rejects. failureOf (:62-66) turns it into a vendor-failure with no costUsd, and job-run.ts books the outcome's cost only `if (!meter.used())` - used is already true. cost-metering golden path, 'Failures are spend': every call that reached the provider gets a row with the failure reason. Fixed: catch inside `live`, book a `failed` row at the estimate (or unpriced with the reason) before rethrowing, so the breaker's retries are visible as spend.

## Flow
- live dojo job on cloud.google; the router's generate throws after Google processed the request (timeout, malformed body)
- metered -> paid rejects -> failureOf -> vendor-failure, retried by the breaker
- spend_rows / spend_unpriced for the step: 0 rows per failed call

## Expected impact
The operator sees what a retry storm on the google stack cost. Could break: a double booking if the router already writes its own ledger row for the same call (check lib/imaging/router before building).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - failed vendor calls are ledger rows
Before: failed calls with a row: 0 of N (walked: metered -> paid -> meter.ts has no catch branch)
After: N of N, outcome `failed` with the error's sentence
Method: simulation - needs a live-mode dojo job over a throwing fake port and a store; the router's own ledger (lib/, another context) must be read first
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/producers/src/dojo/define.ts:79-83
packages/kernel/src/spend/meter.ts:113-130 (entries only from a returned live)
packages/kernel/src/job-run.ts: `if (!meter.used() && cur.mode.kind === "live") chargeOutcome(...)`
instrument: a packages/producers test: live dojo job, ports.generate rejects, count spend rows/unpriced for the step (0 today, 1 per failed call after)

title: A short dojo generate is thrown away and the whole arm re-bought on every breaker retry
body:
## Summary
When Google returns fewer images than `repeats`, packages/producers/src/dojo/define.ts returns a vendor-failure and discards what was paid for; the breaker retries the step, which buys all `count` images again.

## Description
perform (dojo/define.ts:118) returns `{kind: "vendor-failure"}` for `served.value.length !== count` after the metered call settled; nothing is written, so the next plan (dojoGooglePlan, plan.ts:134-149) still sees the arm not whole and the retry generates `count` again, up to the breaker limit. v1's never-re-spend rule (an arm with its PNGs on disk is not re-billed) is defeated by the producer discarding the PNGs it got. Fixed: write the images received (r1..rk), book the step as produced with the shortfall named, and let the plan's per-candidate `have` decide what is still owed - or fail fatal so a human decides, rather than retry-buying.

## Flow
- live dojo cycle, repeats 3; Google returns 2 images for one arm
- perform -> vendor-failure (2 of 3); 2 images billed and dropped
- breaker retry -> generate 3 again; repeated to the breaker limit

## Expected impact
A flaky google arm costs repeats x attempts instead of repeats. Could break: the gate surface's assumption that an arm has all repeats (readbacks plan per candidate already).

## Evaluation
Claim: performance (spend) - images bought per arm on a short answer
Before: walked: 3 x (1 + retries) images billed for one arm whose first answer was short; 2 kept 0
After: 3 billed, 2 kept, 1 owed (or 3 billed and a fatal for a human)
Method: simulation - needs a live-mode job over a fake generate that answers short; not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
packages/producers/src/dojo/define.ts:114-118
packages/producers/src/dojo/plan.ts:137-140 (whole arm regenerated when any candidate is missing)
instrument: a packages/producers test driving defineDojoGoogle live with a generate that returns count-1 images: count generate calls and images billed until the job ends

title: The words landing never writes the words record the domain declares for it
body:
## Summary
lib/producers/words.ts `land` returns `{rev: 0, unchanged: true}`, so the metadata turn's answer never reaches the WORDS step record's `written` field (packages/domain/src/steps/parts.ts:26-37).

## Description
Since L43 the domain declares a words record whose `written` is 'what the metadata turn wrote, so an edit since stays visible'. The producer's binding still says 'the words part holds no step record yet' (lib/producers/words.ts:68) and lands nothing; the answer lives only on the job output, so the words editor cannot show what the turn wrote. aff4a6a3 corrected the definition's header to say this; the behaviour is the binding's.

## Flow
- a words job runs write-words (dry or live)
- the turn's fitted metadata is booked as the job output
- land -> no record write; the words record's `written` stays null

## Expected impact
The words editor shows what the metadata turn wrote. Could break: an editor that treats `written: null` as 'never ran'.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the record holds the turn's answer
Before: landed words jobs whose record carries `written`: 0 of N (land is a no-op)
After: N of N
Method: simulation - lib/producers/words.ts is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/producers/words.ts:68-71  // The words part holds no step record yet ... async land() { return ok({ rev: 0, unchanged: true }); }
packages/domain/src/steps/parts.ts:26-37 WORDS.written
instrument: tests/next-server/producer-step-words-voice.test.ts case: after a dry words job lands, read the part's words record and expect `written` to equal the job output's metadata

title: A local dojo spec with an unknown media is refused with a sentence about google video
body:
## Summary
runnerOf (packages/producers/src/dojo/plan.ts:69-70) and its Python twin (pipeline/foundry/dojo_job.py:77-78) refuse every stack/media pair without a runner as '... - google video has no lane; see the overlay's video section.', including `stack=local media=audio`.

## Description
The refusal is a real error the operator reads on the launch; its second clause names the one missing pair (google/video) even when the stack is local. Fixed: append that clause only for stack google with a video media, both languages, and pin both with a case.

## Flow
- gen-spec stack local, media 'audio'
- runnerOf -> err invalid 'no runner for stack=local media=audio - google video has no lane; ...'

## Expected impact
The refusal names what is actually wrong. Could break: producer-dojo.test.ts's message match, if it pins the long form.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an error sentence that states the actual cause
Before: refusal sentences that misname the cause: 1 of 2 unrunnable classes (local/unknown)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - the Python twin is in pipeline/foundry; changing Node alone splits the twins' words
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: runnerOf({stack:'local',media:'audio'}) message asserted in tests/next-server/producer-dojo.test.ts and the Python twin's selftest
